subject: Architecture
title: Mass Timber: Skyscrapers Made of Wood
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Mass Timber: Skyscrapers Made of Wood.

hook.text: Engineers are building skyscrapers from wood — not because they're nostalgic, but because wood beats steel on carbon.

buildup.text: Cross-laminated timber layers wood at right angles — creating panels as strong as steel but six times lighter.

discovery.text: Trees absorb carbon while growing. Using wood in buildings locks that carbon away for the building's lifetime.

twist.text: Thick mass timber chars on the outside during fire but doesn't burn through — it's actually safer than steel beams.

climax.text: Milwaukee's Ascent tower is 25 stories of mass timber — the tallest timber building in the world in 2022.

punchline.text: The oldest building material. Now the newest skyscraper technology.

quiz.question: Why is mass timber considered better for the climate than steel?
options: It requires less water to manufacture
Trees absorb carbon, and using wood locks it in the building
Timber factories produce zero pollution during manufacturing

details.summary: Mass timber construction uses engineered wood products like CLT and glulam to build structures rivaling concrete and steel in strength. Buildings up to 25 stories have been completed, storing carbon rather than emitting it.
details.whyItMatters: Concrete and steel production generates roughly 11% of global CO2 emissions. Mass timber reverses this equation — trees absorb carbon while growing, and the wood locks it away for the building's lifetime, turning structures into carbon sinks.
takeaways: Engineered wood products rival concrete and steel in strength
Mass timber stores carbon rather than emitting it
Buildings up to 25 stories have been completed in wood

faq.question: Is mass timber safe in fire and earthquakes?
faq.answer: Yes. Mass timber chars predictably at a known rate, maintaining structural integrity far longer than unprotected steel, which softens rapidly at high temperature. In seismic zones, timber's flexibility and light weight are advantages — it absorbs earthquake energy rather than resisting rigidly.

faq.question: Where are the tallest mass timber buildings?
faq.answer: Mjøstårnet in Norway (85 meters), Ascent in Milwaukee (87 meters), and Sara Cultural Centre in Sweden (75 meters) are among the tallest completed timber structures. Proposals for 40+ story timber towers exist in London, Tokyo, and Vancouver.
